drhp.business: The Company designs, manufactures, and retails a portfolio of men's, women's, and kids' apparel and accessories across multiple brands and price points. It operates through a mix of exclusive brand outlets, departmental stores, multi-brand outlets, and e-commerce channels, serving a wide consumer base from mass-premium to premium segments. The business leverages a strong supply chain, omnichannel integration, and a focus on fashion relevance and brand experience.

risks.note: Heightened uncertainty from geopolitical tensions, commodity price spillovers, and elevated inflation expectations create near-term pressure on trade, input costs, and business sentiment.
risks.risk: Geopolitical tensions and commodity price spillovers

risks.note: Spillovers from the West Asia conflict, particularly through higher energy prices, freight costs, and supply-chain disruptions, could increase input costs and weigh on inflation and consumer sentiment in the short term.
Lingering inflation and global uncertainty may keep consumers value-conscious, potentially softening near-term demand momentum in the apparel sector.
Inflationary pressures, uneven discretionary spending, and increasing household debt have affected demand across parts of the Indian apparel market, and demand may remain uneven in the near term.
Global supply-chain disruptions, driven by geopolitical tensions and freight cost volatility, pose a risk to input costs and operational continuity.

sk.overview: India's organised retail comprises organised brick-and-mortar and e-commerce, with e-commerce the fastest-growing format. India retail was ~Rs 83 trillion in FY2025 (~21% organised) and is projected to reach Rs 123-135 trillion by FY2030. India e-commerce (including quick commerce) is ~Rs 6 trillion GMV (~US$70 billion) currently, projected to reach Rs 15-18 trillion (12-13% retail penetration) by FY2030.
